correctness.rationale: For every odd n>=3, two odd rim cycles each force at least one slack edge, so <=3n-2 facet vertices. Equality forces all rungs tight and one slack on each rim; rung differences ±1 force the two slack edges to coincide, and all other gradients satisfy the exact T(z) transitions. The connected tight paths give every counted assignment a genuine facet. Closure is [z^0] of tr(T^(n-1)); eigenvalues z+z^-1±1 and parity yield 2n times the central trinomial. Local CLT gives the asymptotic. A standalone standard-library checker exhaustively generated all normalized edge-1-Lipschitz potentials for n=3,5,7, checked BFS connectedness and agreement with the independent transfer for n<=29. No finite check substitutes for the proof.

originality.rationale: The exact new quantity is the number of maximum-vertex facets on the nonbipartite odd-prism family, not the known general tight-graph characterization or any total facet formula. Direct full-text comparisons with Higashitani–Jochemko–Michałek, D'Alì–Delucchi–Michałek, Braun–Bruegge, and Aliaga show no matching all-odd-n maximum-support classification or the evaluated 2n central-trinomial count. Semantic mathematical-record queries were run for the family, coefficient sequence, aliases, maximal tight-edge count, and possible broader polytope statements. This is best-knowledge originality, not uniqueness certification.
residual_risks: An unindexed or differently named source may have evaluated the odd-prism maximum-support layer using a general root-polytope incidence formula. Search absence does not prove uniqueness.
No independent human bibliographic verification has been conducted.

value.rationale: The maximum number of vertices on a facet and the number of attaining facets form an intrinsic face-incidence invariant of the real transportation unit ball. The odd-prism family is a canonical nonbipartite cylindrical metric, forcing an exact two-slack parity obstruction unlike bipartite planar flow cases. The theorem resolves the sharp upper bound, gives an equality classification and closed all-dimensional central-trinomial multiplicity, rather than an arbitrary finite census or an unevaluated general criterion.
